content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file in one pass without tool feedback, so I'm being careful about API correctness while designing an ancient treant in Warcraft style—chunky build, huge hands, broad shoulders, bark face with glowing eyes, an antler-branch crown, mossy shoulders, and root-like feet, standing roughly 4.2 meters tall to really tower over a human.

I'm planning the skeleton: hips root joint, a spine chain rising through chest to a short neck and head, shoulders with arms extended outward in a T-pose-ish rest stance, and thick trunk-like legs ending in root feet, plus separate jaw joints for the mouth. I want to stick to APIs I'm confident in—chains with catmull paths, sweeps, lofts, spikes, sprouts, and basic primitive parts—while planning leaf cards via textured geometry and glowing eye/rune accents, then I'm working out exact joint coordinates for hips, knees, and ankles to build the leg chains.

Now I'm reasoning through how chain tips work with catmull paths versus polylines, then designing the tapering trunk-like legs and root-foot toes as small sweeps curving down from the ankle to touch the floor with tapered radii.

For the feet, I'm planning a flattened sole pad as a scaled sphere positioned so its bottom just barely sinks into the floor plane, keeping within acceptable tolerance. Then I'm moving on to the torso, lofting it along a spine chain curving from hips to chest using a catmull path.

Figuring out the joint hierarchy, I decide to make a separate root "pelvis" joint and chain the spine joints off it, using four names for a three-span path so the tip lands at the chest. Now I'm setting up the sweep along that spine with a radius function controlling the belly and chest widths.

I'm giving the chest broader side radii than the belly for a stockier upper body, keeping the front-back radius symmetrical, and going with a 10-sided section for a slightly chunky bark-like silhouette while still using smooth shading overall.

Now I'm designing a custom bark paint function that stretches noise and cell patterns vertically to create plate-like bark textures, blending light, mid, dark, and moss tones based on cell edges and upward-facing normals for mottling.

I'm adding hand-painted, Warcraft-style lighting: warm highlights on upward-facing surfaces and cool shadows on downward ones, plus moss accents on faces tilted enough toward the sky.

Thinking about texel density for the paint sheet now—at 1024px over a treant's roughly 60m² surface I get around 9mm per texel, which should be fine, but I'm weighing whether to bump the paint size to 2048 for sharper detail without risking the texture atlas overflowing and auto-shrinking.

I'll go with 2048; the 4096 atlas ceiling should still accommodate it alongside the other card textures, though there's some render-speed tradeoff to accept. I also need to stay under the 1000-part limit, so I'm planning to merge small pieces where I can—starting the build with a torso sweep from the hips with rounded caps, then chaining leg sweeps with thigh and knee radii including a knotted bump at the knee.

Now I'm roughing out the rest pose and limb geometry: legs apart, arms extended outward in an A-pose with approximate joint coordinates for shoulder, elbow, and wrist, tapering radii along the arm. For the hands I'm sketching oversized palms with root-like finger sweeps—five digits per hand with multiple joints each, keeping the joint budget in mind as I plan the finger chains.

Still defining finger chains...

Now I'm placing the wrist position and working out the palm center offset, with the hand hanging down and outward so fingers splay forward, down, and slightly apart across the palm width.

Figuring out the forearm direction and finger extension, then setting up a mirrored helper function so left and right hands can share the same positioning logic with a sign flip on x.

Now I'm planning the shoulder geometry: mossy burl humps with sprouting branches and leaf cards, plus oversized bark-plate pauldrons for a Warcraft-style exaggerated silhouette. Then I move to the head, placing the neck chain joints from the base up to where the skull will attach.

For the head itself, I'm envisioning a craggy treant face with a broad brow ridge, deep-set glowing amber-green eyes, a knotted branch-like nose, a wide jaw, and a beard made of hanging moss and roots.

I'll build a small helper function that takes left/up/forward offsets and calls head.local accordingly, assuming negative values simply sum to produce the opposite direction.

For skull parts attached to the head bone, since the pose is fixed at build time and the head is only slightly tilted, I'll just use world-space axes with a forward direction like [0, 0.12, 1] for simplicity.

Actually, I realize I'll keep it simpler by setting the head's dir explicitly to [0,0,1] so it matches world up, and define offsets as plain model coordinates relative to a constant head position rather than relying on local tilt math. Now I'm starting the cranium geometry as a scaled sphere positioned near the top of the head with bark-colored paint.

For the face, I'm working out angled brow capsules on each side that slant downward toward the nose to give the treant a stern, ancient expression, positioning them symmetrically above where the eyes will go.

Now I'm designing deep-set eyes with glowing amber orbs: dark sockets made from scaled spheres, a small glowing ellipsoid eye inside with a warm "#ffd23a" glow, plus a tiny dark pupil box and heavy bark eyelids for depth.

I'm shaping the knotty nose as a swept capsule from brow to upper lip with small nostril knobs, adding cheekbone spheres, and blocking out the upper jaw as a tapered frustum box, while planning a dark cracked mouth interior with chunky wooden "teeth" blocks and a separate jointed lower jaw.

For the lower jaw and chin I'm placing another tapered frustum bone with a heavy chin sphere, a dark interior box between the jaws, and a few wedge-shaped teeth cones. For the beard, I'm imagining moss-card textures mixed with hanging root-vine sweeps attached to the jaw bone, aiming for around seven varied strands trailing down toward the chest.

Ears can be flat leaf-shaped extrudes flaring out and back from the sides of the skull, and for the crown I'm thinking of antler-like branch sweeps sprouting from the head bone, each side splitting into tines topped with leaf clusters, plus a mossy cap and tiny mushrooms scattered across the cranium. For the back, I want two large limbs arcing up from the shoulders into a leafy canopy overhead.

Simplest approach for the canopy is low-poly icosahedron "puffs" for a stylized Warcraft-style leaf mass, flat-shaded with a green paint gradient and leaf cards scattered on the surface, rising about a meter above the head. Aiming for a total height around 5 meters for the whole treant, with roughly 4.1 meters from the ground to the top of the head and the branches/canopy filling out the rest.

I'm designing leaf textures as small SVG shapes with visible veins in two or three green tones plus an autumn orange-gold accent, picked randomly for variety, then scattering dozens of leaf cards across each canopy puff mounted on rigid bones at the branch joints. For the branches themselves, I'm setting up a curved bone chain rooted at the back of the shoulders that sweeps upward and outward.

I'm reconsidering overall scale since treant proportions should feel towering — adjusting so the body runs floor to shoulder around 3.0, head top near 4.0, branches reaching 4.4, and canopy topping out near 4.8, with branches curving outward from the shoulders so they clear the head, and small antler-like branches on the head reaching up toward 4.5.

For the canopy, I'm placing larger leaf puffs at the branch tips and smaller ones in the middle. I'm also thinking through decorative details: hanging roots on the back, vines spiraling around the forearms using a helix curve, and thorny vine wraps instead of metal trims to keep it nature-themed. For a magical touch, I want a glowing rune circle or sap-crack decal on the chest, applying emissive glow to a textured decal part so the rune pattern actually lights up.

To place the decal correctly, I need to find the right surface point on the torso using the nearest-surface-hit function, which always returns a valid hit, so I can anchor the decal there without risking a null crash. I also need to make sure the decal's generated material qualifies for the glow effect to work properly.

I'm thinking about adding more organic detail -- glowing sap veins in gold-green along the body, a hollow chest knothole with a glowing core echoing a fantasy lantern motif, and amber glowing eyes, plus scattering small bark-colored knots and burls across the torso and limbs as separate stick parts for texture.

I want to keep the part budget manageable, around 500 total, so I'm planning limited counts: roughly 14 burls on the torso, 6 per leg, plus about 20 cone-shaped broken branch stubs with pale cut rings scattered across the body. I'm also adding small bracket fungus clusters (lathe caps on stalks, orange and red) on the shoulders and thighs for a saturated accent, and starting on moss patches for a cape using flat card geometry.

Now I'm sketching out the moss, flower, and vine decorations: scattering moss tufts on upward-facing surfaces of the shoulders and head, adding ten small flower cards on the shoulders, and working out how to wrap ivy vines spiraling around the forearms and legs by sweeping a helical path skinned to the arm bone chain, which requires computing local perpendicular frames along each limb segment.

Working out vine frame generation...

Defining the radius taper functions for limbs, and planning to reuse a single bark paint object across torso, limbs, and head so the pattern reads as continuous, with subtle lighter accents for wear.

I'm sketching out the treant's palette now — deep browns and shadowed bark tones for the body, warm gold highlights, and layered green moss and leaf colors for the foliage accents.

Writing bark paint function...

Still refining bark shading...

Now I'm figuring out moss placement, blending it onto upward-facing surfaces and shoulder areas using noise-driven thresholds, then coloring it by mixing dark and light moss tones with a subtle highlight on top.

I'm also adding mud blending near the feet where height is low, and sprinkling in sparse dim amber specks along seams to suggest painted golden sap veins without relying on any glow effects. The head reuses the bark treatment but with more face-lighting, while mouth interior details stay flat, simple colors.

Now I'm nailing down concrete body proportions in meters: hip, knee, and ankle joint positions for the legs, then extending toe chains forward from each ankle with two joints per toe for the digits.

I'll add gnarly root tendrils sweeping outward from each foot down to the floor, five per foot, tapering and rigid off the ankle bone for that twisted root look.

Now I'm setting up the torso spine chain from pelvis through chest, defining the control points and a radius-shaping function that widens from narrow hips and waist to a broader chest and shoulders.

Now I'm thinking through the torso-hip transition, making sure the pelvis radius tapers correctly into the leg joints at the hip, and considering adding a loincloth or waist band detail made of moss or vines.

I'm designing a braided vine belt with a glowing amber gem buckle, placed by finding a loop around the spine's second joint and sweeping it into a closed band, then positioning the gem buckle at the front using the nearest surface point. I'm also considering a second diagonal vine bandolier crossing the chest.

Working out the belt coordinates...

I continue plotting the remaining loop points around the torso into a closed catmull curve, checking the drape stays plausible for a closed path. I weigh whether to add a bandolier strap for that Warcraft feel, deciding it's worth the moderate risk.

Skipping acorn charms along the vine for now; instead I sketch out a chunky chest plate made from overlapping extruded bark plates with bevels, giving it a mossy brown finish and positioning it over the chest for that heavy armored look.

Actually extrude could work better, placing the plate's thickness axis along the chest's forward direction, but I need to account for how the torso curves outward -- near the edges the surface recedes, so a flat plate would float off the surface unless I offset its z-position to match the curvature at that x location.

I'll skip the tilt and keep plate thickness centered so it embeds half in, half out of the surface. To keep things manageable, I'll limit to two pectoral plates, maybe three stacked belly plates, and some ridge detailing using surface loops traced around the torso at different heights.

For the ridges, I'm checking that loop radii near the shoulder don't collide with the arm geometry, confirming the smallest valid loop stays on the torso surface only. Then I'll move on to defining the neck chain connecting the torso up to the head center point.

Now I'm sketching the neck as a short, thick tapering path with decreasing radii, naming the joints "neck1" and "neck2" with the head joint placed at the top. I'm also working out the head dimensions—cranium radius, chin position, and how the head overlaps the neck and torso top—to get the vertical proportions right.

I'm realizing the round cap on the torso's end is too large, pushing the shoulder dome up too high toward the neck, so I'm reworking the taper radii and considering flat caps or separate shoulder spheres to keep the proportions correct.

A flat top cap at the torso covered by a trapezius sphere works better, with legs split apart leaving an empty crotch gap handled as a root-skirt, and I'm thinking of adding a loincloth of moss or vines hanging from the belt to fill that space visually.

Reworking proportions: torso now spans 1.75 to 3.1, shoulders at 3.0, with head center positioned forward and up around 3.72-3.75 so it thrusts heroically beyond the chest line. Antlers plus canopy puffs push the total height to roughly 5 meters, which fits the scale of an ancient treant.

Now I'm sketching the arms with heroic proportions: shoulder, elbow, and wrist coordinates giving a long upper arm and thick forearm tapering slightly toward the wrist, with hands spanning about 0.4m. I'm checking that the shoulder joint sits properly relative to the torso radius so it doesn't poke outside unnaturally.

I'm placing shoulder humps as spheres that stay rigid with the arm bone so they move together, with moss texture painted on top, and I'm working out the hand geometry—positioning the palm along the forearm direction as a flattened ellipsoid with its own local axes for width, length, and thickness.

Now I'm working out finger placement, spreading four fingers plus a thumb across the palm's width, with offsets mirrored for left versus right hands so the thumb sits on the inner side closer to the body.

Still shaping finger geometry...

Now I'm naming the finger and toe joint chains with side-prefixed identifiers like fing{S}{i}a/b/c and toe{S}{i}a/b/c, then setting up the leg chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints and figuring out parenting back to the pelvis.

For the leg chain, pelvis acts as the parent joint, while the arm chain parents to the chest (spine tip) instead. I'm working out the skin radius profile for the leg so it tapers from thigh to ankle with a knee bump, keeping things simple with scalar values rather than asymmetric pairs.

I'm figuring out how to reference the ankle joint as the chain's tip for attaching the foot sole, settling on using the last entry in the joints array since the tip joint is included there.

For the arms I'm naming the joints shoulder, elbow, and wrist per side. For the back branches, I'm defining a chain parented to the chest with a path curving upward and outward through four named points, tapering radius from 0.2 to 0.08, and planning sprout sub-branches with zero count so they stay rigid on the bone rather than jointed.

Working out how to attach twig sweeps rigidly to the branch bone, using the branch's frame position at a given t as the starting point and binding them to the branch joint so they move together...

For the actual twig layout, I'm planning three twigs per main branch, each tipped with a small flat-shaded icosahedron leaf puff, painted with a gradient that lightens toward the top based on normal direction.

To keep part counts manageable, I'm batching all the leaf card scatter hits across every puff into a single call per texture rather than per-puff, so with three leaf textures that's just three parts total instead of dozens.

For the canopy paint, I want a faceted gradient coloring leaves from light yellow-green at the top to darker tones at the bottom, mixed with noise for mottling and occasional golden highlights, using flat shading for the faceted look -- cards themselves will just use their texture colors without tinting. For the leaf shape itself I'm sketching an SVG outline with a curved leaf silhouette, a lighter midrib line, and a darker edge.

I'm planning three leaf color variants -- a green with light vein highlights, a bright yellow-green, and a golden autumn tone with subtle mixing. I'm also sketching textures for moss tufts as grass-like blades, hanging lichen as tassel shapes, and flowers as five-petal rotated ellipse clusters sized small for shoulder placement, plus starting on mushroom cap shapes to scatter on hits.

Writing mushroom and fungi geometry...

Thinking about shelf fungus shape as a half-cylinder disc, like a flattened D-shape jutting outward from the trunk with its flat face oriented along the surface normal.

Working out the rotation math...

For embedding the half-disc shelf fungus into the trunk surface, I'll offset it inward along the normal and pass the hit frame directly as the `at` point so it inherits the correct bone weights automatically. Shelf fungus seems like a nice detail to include, so I'll add it.

I also want to keep things compact with a scatter helper that filters hits and applies randomness, while being careful not to leave unused imports around since that'll trip up type checking later. Beyond that, I'm thinking about extra face details like eyebrow moss and wooden teeth, plus a glowing rune decal for the chest and amber rune bands on the forearms, sketched as a small glowing glyph texture.

Writing SVG code...

I'm also considering adding floating firefly-like particles drifting around the treant for extra atmosphere.

Setting up imports for the builder script...

Setting up the metadata object and palette constants, then writing the leaf texture as an SVG path shape...

Still writing SVG textures...

Now I'm sketching the helper functions and builder scaffolding for the treant model, starting with coordinate helpers and the pelvis joint setup.

Building the spine chain next, rooted at the pelvis with spine1 through chest joints along a curved catmull path, then double-checking the joint count matches the number of names provided.

Next I'm defining the neck chain with two segments off the chest, then attaching the head joint at the end of the neck with a forward-facing direction vector.

For the jaw, I'm placing its pivot near the skull base and aiming it forward-down to form the hinge. I'm setting the head center position and establishing a helper function to place all head parts relative to that center, with face depth extending forward along z.

Now I'm sizing the cranium sphere and checking its coverage against the jaw pivot and neck junction, then shaping the face mass as a frustum block covering the muzzle and brow with heavier cheek width tapering toward the nose.

Positioning dark eye sockets as small spheres protruding slightly past the cranium surface, with glowing eye orbs nested inside them and a brow ridge capsule arching above to reach even further forward.

Now I'm placing a thin pupil slit box just inside the glowing eye sphere's front face, then sketching a curved catmull-rom path for the nose bridge running from the brow down to a protruding tip, using tapering radii to shape the bone.

Nostril knobs, cheek bulges, and the mouth area are next -- a dark cavity box for the mouth, small cone teeth up top, curved tusk-like lower fangs, and a frustum-shaped lower jaw block.

I'm positioning a chin knot sphere and double-checking that the jaw doesn't clip into the neck or mouth cavity. Then I'm adding a beard made of mossy root strands sweeping from the chin downward and outward, plus hanging lichen cards and long whisker-like roots near the nostrils for extra texture.

Now I'm writing a custom moss paint shader that blends dark and light moss tones using noise and surface normal direction, with shadow blending on the underside...

Next I'm plotting the main antler branches curving up from the skull using bark-colored tapering radii, then adding smaller tines along each branch using interpolated points on a catmull-rom path...

Checking the overall height: antler tips with leaf puffs should cap around 5 meters total, so I'm adjusting the y-offsets of the branch control points down slightly to keep the tree within that limit.

Now I'm working out the ears -- leaf-shaped outlines positioned sideways and slightly back on the head, using a small set of outline points to define a pointed leaf silhouette that I'll extrude with some smoothing to give them thickness.

Now I'm working on the shoulders, adding bone joints and an oversized Warcraft-style shoulder pad using a scaled sphere positioned at the shoulder, painted bark-colored, with a slightly larger moss-colored cap layered over the upper half.

Calculating the exact hemisphere geometry for the moss cap, positioning it relative to the bark sphere so the moss dome sits just below the bark's top point, tuning the scale values so both pieces fit together without clipping.

Then I'm thinking about adding broken-branch spikes jutting from the shoulder like thorns, evoking classic Warcraft-style shoulder armor with sprout-like protrusions around the shoulder surface.

For the rest, I'm planning chest decals, burls scattered on the torso via a sweep with exclusion zones, and checking that scatter operations on sweeps stay performant. I also need moss, vines, and leaf cards, and I'm roughly tallying part counts — torso, two legs, two arms, palms, fingers with knuckle spheres, and toes — landing somewhere around 30+ parts for the hands alone.

Adding in roots, head geometry, branches, puffs, stub/burls, fungus, and leaf cards brings the total part count to roughly 350, which feels reasonable, and with ~600 leaf cards across the puffs that's about 2400 triangles, still fine. Now I'm working out wrist detailing — adding root-like cuffs by cutting a loop across the arm sweep at a point near the wrist, using the tangent direction from the arm's chain to orient the cut correctly.

I'm planning cuff loops at the forearm and similar joints (ankle, knee) using a small lift and rope-like sweep radius with a vine color, two per arm and three per leg, while checking that the cutting plane only intersects the arm/leg surface and not accidentally the torso. The resulting loop path should inherit the arm's skinning weights so the rope sweep follows the joint's deformation naturally.

Now I'm sketching a helix helper that walks along a path, building a local frame from the tangent to compute perpendicular offset vectors, then spiraling points around the path using cosine/sine functions scaled by a radius function and phase—this will drive the vine's spiral geometry around limbs.

With that helper in place, I'm wiring the vine sweeps to use the chain's curve directly, confirming bones can take a Chain reference, and setting the vine's tube radius to track the limb's radius plus a small offset so it hugs the arm or leg naturally. Then I'm planning to gather leaf card frames by sampling angles along each vine's sweep, collecting around eight per vine into a shared array for placing the leaf cards afterward.

Now I'm figuring out the canopy leaves: I'll scatter around 520 points across the combined puff surfaces with a minimum distance of 0.07 so leaves don't crowd or bury inside neighboring meshes, then size the leaf cards and set their bend/lean so each card generates roughly 16 triangles with cross-faces, keeping total triangle count comfortably under the 60k limit.

I'm also planning to build the puff clusters themselves using a small icosahedron geometry for each puff, flat-shaded and colored with the leaf paint, then writing a helper function that places a main puff plus two satellite puffs at each branch tip and twig location to create denser foliage clusters along both sides of the tree.

For the leaf coloring, I'm defining a paint function that blends dark and light leaf tones based on noise and surface normal, adds a gold highlight near the top-facing surfaces, and darkens the underside with a shadow tint -- giving each puff a faceted, hand-painted look.

I'm skipping the idea of a root cape hanging off the shoulders and instead scattering small bark-covered burl stubs across the torso surface, placing embedded spheres with slight flattening at random points above a height threshold where the surface faces outward.

Writing stub geometry...

Adding stick options and paint for the cap, plus a shelf fungus helper and moss tufts scattered across upward-facing surfaces using filtered frame hits.

Scattering flowers across the same surfaces with a pink/white/yellow color palette, then moving on to code the legs and beard geometry with closures over the builder object.

Writing beard tip coordinates...

Actually I realize the beard strands as positioned would intersect the chest geometry at that z-depth, so I need to push them forward of the chest surface instead.

For hanging lichen on the beard strands, I'm sampling frames along each strand to place cards that droop downward rather than standing perpendicular, using a hanging-lichen texture at small scale.

Now I'm layering in facial details: heavy eyelid capsules above each eye, mossy brow sweeps with thin radius capsules colored like moss, bark-style face paint across the head, and positioning lower tusks emerging beside the upper lip with a sweep from jaw level upward.

Still working out tusk placement...

Instead of full teeth, I'm opting for a simple row of six small rectangular dark-wood teeth boxes along the inner rim of the lower jaw, spaced evenly and positioned to peek above the chin line.

Deciding to skip visible lower teeth since they'd be hidden inside the mouth cavity, and instead adding two downward-pointing upper fangs near the face. For the arms, I'm sketching out the wrist/palm sphere and considering whether to add bark-plate bracer bands on the forearm, but settling on just keeping the loop bands with an outward-facing rune decal placed partway along the arm's outer curve.

Working out the decal placement math -- offsetting a point outward from the arm sweep, finding the nearest surface hit, and setting decal size and glow intensity, then noting a chest rune decal and deciding to skip a lighter belly patch. I'm also planning a waist vine belt with a gem buckle and considering leg bark bands with darker moss/mud paint near the feet.

Next I'm adding knee wraps along the legs, then giving the head trailing moss-colored root strands like a mane down the back. I'm also sketching dorsal bark ridge spikes running along the spine using the sweep's frame angles, working out how the spike function takes a base point, direction, length, and radius with an explicit bark color.

Writing branch chain code...

Still writing twig geometry...

I'm double checking that the canopy doesn't obscure the head and that the whole mesh rests properly on the ground, with feet and toes grounded at floor level.

Writing toe positioning logic...

Still defining toe joint positions...

Counting up total joints across toes, fingers, legs, arms, spine, neck, head, and branches gives roughly 78, well under the 160 limit. For the toe sweep, I'm using a chain-based bone sweep with a given radius to build the geometry.

I'm adding a small claw spike at each toe tip, angled downward and forward, and a heel/root sweep running from the ankle back toward the foot's underside, rigged to the ankle joint.

Now I'm generating four root tendrils per foot curving outward from the ankle at different angles with tapering radii, though I'm noticing these might overlap with the toes, so I should offset their angles to diagonal positions instead.

That gives four toes per foot, eight parts total, with mud and moss painted near the feet. Now I'm setting up the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions for each arm symmetrically.

Defining arm chain and taper radii...

Working out finger lengths and offsets, mirroring the x-axis offset based on left versus right hand so fingers spread inward correctly.

Still defining finger curl geometry...

Finishing the thumb joint positions and adding knuckle spheres sized to match. I'm checking palm color and scale, deciding to skip claws and leaf buds for simplicity, and verifying the frustum box helper orients width/height correctly for forward-pointing shapes. For the face I'm weighing whether to add painted details like warpaint or moss but leaning toward keeping it simple.

I'm reusing the bark paint for most parts while giving vines a solid darker green, and double-checking that colors can be either strings or paint objects. For the chest I'm working out pec plate geometry using extrusion with a pentagon-shield outline and smoothing.

I realize the torso's curved surface means the plate's outer edges will float noticeably away from the body since the surface drops off faster than the flat plate does, so I need to account for that offset.

That could carve raised pectoral ridges by draping a closed outline near the chest surface, letting points snap to the nearest surface so the sweep hugs the contour properly.

Now I'm moving to final checks: skip the mane/fur idea and the body glow sap lines, then just write all the actual code, making sure glow effects apply correctly to both decal parts and sweep meshes before handling the eye glow part.

Checking belt placement—it's sitting a bit high on the torso, closer to waist than hip, so I'll adjust so it doesn't intersect the arms, finding the nearest surface point for the gem attachment and setting the belt rope thickness to a thin radius.

I'm figuring out how to hang decorative vine cards along the belt path, using `along()` to generate points and orienting each frame to face upward rather than along the belt's tangent direction so the cards hang naturally.

For the hanging beard strands, I'll sample points along each strand and build frames from them so weighting inherits correctly from the explicit bone. Then I'm thinking through the texture count: separate atlas tiles for hanging moss, tufts, flowers, and leaves, each as its own mesh part.

Writing TypeScript helper logic...

Writing bark paint function...

Still blending moss color...

I'm also adding a subtle gold sap vein along seams for detail, and confirming the bark color definitions and nested puff arrays work correctly for scattering surface elements.

Checking the head joint parenting and attachment points against the API, then moving on to writing the leg chain structure...

I'm building the leg chain using a catmull-rom path through hip, knee, and ankle points, parented to the pelvis, then sweeping it with a tapering profile in bark color. I'm also adding a knee burl detail as a small sphere at the knee position.

Now I'm adding cuffs at the ankle and knee using skin loops along the leg's parametric length, plus wrist cuffs on the arms, before assembling everything into the final build function with the bark material and RNG setup.

Writing torso sweep...

I'm working out the torso's shoulder and chest placement relative to the spine bone, making sure the flat end cap at the top aligns with the neck radius starting point so the transition looks seamless.

Now I'm planning spike placements along the dorsal side of the torso's spine, spacing five bark-colored ridges running up the back like a tree trunk's spine. Moving on to writing out the shoulder geometry code next.

Setting up puff clusters for mossy foliage...

I should always pass a bone option explicitly when drawing capsules so endpoints anchor to the right joint rather than defaulting to the nearest one. Now I'm sketching the flower geometry with petals arranged around a center point.

Writing SVG code...

Still writing SVG paths...

Now I'm adding mane strands at the back of the head, then moving on to construct the mouth interior box and the frustum-shaped face block with bark coloring, scaled appropriately for the head bone.

Writing extrude code...

I need to annotate the ear points with the proper outline type to avoid inference issues, then move on to the vine helix over the arm with its radius profile and leaf frame placement along each sweep.

I'll push the vine sweep frames into a separate array and give vine leaves their own smaller-sized card call rather than merging with the canopy leaves, to keep sizing distinct even though it costs a few more parts. Now I'm writing the final file, starting with legs needing their own vine helix too.

Checking that the radius profile function and sweep calls type-check correctly, then defining a small `twig` helper that sweeps a Catmull-Rom curve through given points with a tapering radius and a pointed end cap, used for branch-end twig clusters and puffs.

I'm working out the twig tip geometry by sampling a point along the branch path and building a small curve from base to mid to tip with slight offsets for variation, then adding a puff at the tip. For antlers, I'm sweeping a tapered path from a catmull curve through the antler points, adding tines branching off around the 40% and 70% marks with their own twigs and puffs, and finishing up the final root return.

Skipping the shoulder vines idea for now and moving on to writing the moss cap on the head using a scaled sphere hemisphere, plus similar moss hemispheres over the shoulders using a partial sphere geometry pushed into the moss parts array. I'm also filtering those moss parts by upward-facing normals to scatter tufts and flowers, then double-checking the surface call and the hit point vector before writing everything out.
